## Tours through El Chaltén: two ways to experience Patagonia's mountains

[El Chaltén](/argentina/place/el-chalten/) stands in the northern part of [Los Glaciares National Park](/argentina/place/los-glaciares-national-park/), at the foot of the granite massifs of Fitz Roy and Cerro Torre. Visitors come for hiking trails through lenga forests, river valleys and rocky slopes. Even a short stay here feels very different from a day at Perito Moreno Glacier.

Here we have gathered {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} whose main itineraries include El Chaltén. The key question when choosing is **how much time is dedicated specifically to hiking and how independently you want to choose the trails**. Comparing total tour durations without considering mountain days would be misleading: a 13-day tour may provide a more clearly defined hiking programme than a 26-day journey.

For the town's history and its natural setting, visit the [El Chaltén page](/argentina/place/el-chalten/). Here we focus on choosing a real journey, the number of hiking days, travel between towns and preparation for physical activity. More active options are collected under [Argentina adventure tours](/interests/adventure/tours/argentina/).

## Comparing the available itineraries

### 13 days: Laguna Capri and Laguna de los Tres on separate days

The [13-day Argentina, Chile and Patagonia tour](/multi-country/tour/argentina-chile-patagonia-13-days/) introduces travellers to different parts of Los Glaciares in sequence. They first see [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/) from [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/). Then the hiking days around Fitz Roy begin.

**Day 7:** transfer to El Chaltén and a hike to [Laguna Capri](/argentina/place/laguna-capri/). This is a suitable first encounter with the mountains: the walk offers views of Fitz Roy and a chance to assess how you feel before the longer following day. Time is allocated for the ascent, mountain views and the return.

**Day 8:** a full day of trekking to [Laguna de los Tres](/argentina/place/laguna-de-los-tres/). The route passes through Patagonian forest and the Río Blanco valley, with a demanding final section. The panorama of granite peaks rewards the long walk. This is the day to examine particularly carefully if you are planning your first extended mountain hike.

**Day 9:** a transfer to Chile through Patagonian landscapes. The mountains of El Chaltén are therefore part of a closely scheduled sequence of "glacier — two hiking days — Chile", with little additional free time.

This tour suits travellers who want to know their principal hiking objectives in advance and are prepared for a full active day. The inclusion of Laguna de los Tres does not, on its own, guarantee a fixed walking pace, a specific guide or the ability to complete the trail in any weather. These conditions must be confirmed separately.

### 26 days: independent trails and optional kayaking

The [26-day grand journey through Argentina and Patagonia](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/) takes another approach. After visiting the glaciers, travellers arrive in El Chaltén on **day 19**. **Day 20** is reserved for independent hikes, with trails chosen according to the weather and individual fitness. On **day 21**, there is time for further walks before returning to El Calafate. Kayaking is mentioned as an optional paid activity.

This arrangement offers more freedom but also places more responsibility for planning walks on the traveller. It works well if you prefer to choose a trail on arrival, based on the forecast and how you feel. If you want an itinerary that sets out hikes to particular lakes in advance, the 13-day tour is more structured.

If choosing kayaking, check how it fits around the return transfer. Its mention in the programme does not mean it is an obligatory part of the paid package.

| Criterion | 13 days | 26 days |
|---|---|---|
| [Itinerary](/multi-country/tour/argentina-chile-patagonia-13-days/) | Specific hikes on set days | [Independent walks](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-patagonia-26-days/) |
| Main focus | Laguna Capri and Laguna de los Tres | Choose trails locally |
| After El Chaltén | Transfer to Chile | Return to El Calafate |
| Kayaking | Not listed as compulsory | Available separately |

Duration and price information comes from the current listings for these tours:

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_argentina_chili_i_prekrasnaya_patagoniya,tour_source_vsya_argentina}}

## Laguna Capri or Laguna de los Tres: which to choose?

[Laguna Capri](/argentina/place/laguna-capri/) is a trail where you can already see Fitz Roy and become familiar with Patagonian paths without committing to a full day of strenuous hiking. The trail climbs from the village through vegetation and opens onto views of the massif. For many travellers, it makes sense as the first day in El Chaltén.

[Laguna de los Tres](/argentina/place/laguna-de-los-tres/) requires more serious preparation. The hike is longer and its final ascent over rocky ground is substantially harder than an easy walk to a viewpoint. According to the national park administration, the route towards Fitz Roy and Laguna de los Tres is a multi-hour trek of moderate to high difficulty. The duration depends on the starting point, trail conditions and the group.

Both lakes lie in the Fitz Roy area, but they are **different destinations**. One trail should not be substituted for the other when comparing tours. If Laguna de los Tres is too demanding, shorter paths and viewpoints offer alternatives. That choice fits naturally into a free day on the 26-day itinerary; on the 13-day journey, the intended route is already specified.

El Chaltén also offers views of Cerro Torre, the Fitz Roy River valley and other walking destinations. Mentioning them as possible excursions does not mean they are automatically included in an Ada Tours itinerary. Check the actual plan for each day.

## El Chaltén and El Calafate: why visit both?

The two towns belong to the same national park but offer access to **different parts of it**. From [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/), travellers primarily visit [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/), the viewing platforms and excursions on [Lake Argentino](/argentina/place/lake-argentino/). El Chaltén is the starting point for trails beneath Fitz Roy and Cerro Torre.

According to the national park administration, approximately 200 km of road separate the towns. In practice, this is a distinct transfer rather than a short extension of a hike. On the 13-day tour it comes between the glacier day and the first mountain walks; on the 26-day journey separate outward and return transfers are scheduled.

If your main goal is to see a glacier without lengthy hikes, compare [tours through El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/tour/). If hiking is your priority, start by comparing how many full days each itinerary allows in El Chaltén itself. This avoids choosing a long tour that offers only a transit stop beside the mountains.

## Weather and hiking preparation

Weather changes quickly in El Chaltén. Strong winds, rain, low clouds and cold temperatures occur even during the season with long daylight hours. Views of Fitz Roy depend on cloud cover, so a photograph of its summit cannot be promised on a particular date. Summer usually offers more convenient conditions for long hikes, but good weather is never guaranteed.

In winter and the shoulder seasons, snow, ice and mud make trails more difficult. The park administration warns about special equipment requirements in colder weather, registration for certain mountain activities and the need to check trail closures. Conditions change, so relying on old trip reports as a guide to current access is unsafe.

For a long hike, bring trekking shoes with reliable grip, windproof and waterproof layers, drinking water, food and enough time to return before dark. Trails lack normal urban facilities. Assess your experience and follow current ranger guidance before setting out. This preparation is especially important for Laguna de los Tres.

Think also about who will accompany you. A free day for independent walking does not mean an instructor is present on every trail. If you need a guide or a pre-booked private outing, check the confirmed options for the specific tour or excursion.

## Can other activities be added?

One standalone Ada Tours product is [kayaking in El Chaltén](/argentina/el-chalten/el-chalten-kayaking/). It is a different way to explore the area, with its own weather conditions, equipment and operating arrangements. It may appeal to travellers who have already spent time on the hiking trails.

It is important to distinguish a listed excursion from an activity actually included in a tour day. On the 26-day itinerary, kayaking is an **optional activity**. The presence of a [kayaking excursion](/argentina/el-chalten/el-chalten-kayaking/) in the catalogue does not mean it is automatically organised or paid for on every journey through El Chaltén.

For additional natural areas, compare [Argentina wildlife and nature tours](/interests/wildlife/tours/argentina/) and [adventure itineraries](/interests/adventure/tours/argentina/). These catalogues may combine El Chaltén with glaciers, lakes and other regions, but the main hiking days must still be checked in each tour programme.

## Frequently asked questions about tours through El Chaltén

### Which tour is better for a first visit to El Chaltén?

If you want two famous lake hikes planned in advance, choose the 13-day tour with days at Laguna Capri and Laguna de los Tres. If you prefer to select trails according to the weather and your preparation, consider the 26-day journey with free days. This difference matters more than the overall duration of the trip.

### Do I have to hike to Laguna de los Tres?

No. The El Chaltén area offers trails of varying lengths and difficulty. However, the particular 13-day itinerary lists Laguna de los Tres as a dedicated hiking day. If you do not intend to complete it, the programme needs to be discussed with that change in mind.

### Can Fitz Roy and Perito Moreno be combined?

Yes. Both featured tours pass through El Calafate and El Chaltén. The glacier and the mountain trails are in different sectors of the national park, so travelling between them is necessary. Allow separate excursion days for each.

### Are hikes in El Chaltén guided?

That depends on the specific programme and selected services. The 26-day itinerary expressly describes independent walks. The 13-day tour specifies particular hikes, while guiding and other included services must be checked in its listing. A trail name does not automatically guarantee a private guide.

### Are trails open throughout the year?

Access to a specific trail cannot be guaranteed for any given date. The park operates in different seasons, but snow, ice, wind and temporary restrictions affect hiking conditions. Check official park notices immediately before setting out.

### How many nights should I plan in El Chaltén?

A single hike requires at least its own full walking day, separate from transfers. For two different hikes, it is sensible to allow two full days and account for travel time. More time is useful for independent planning, but the exact number of nights depends on the itinerary and schedule.

Choose a tour according to the activity that matters most. For Fitz Roy, the number of hiking days, difficulty of the trails and weather contingency time are decisive. The length of a major journey alone says little about how much of Patagonia you will explore on foot.

## El Pedral in Argentina: penguins, an estancia and Patagonia's coast

El Pedral (Estancia El Pedral) lies in the Punta Ninfas area on the Atlantic coast of Chubut Province. Here the dry Patagonian steppe reaches pebble beaches, while a colony of Magellanic penguins lives near a historic estancia. This is a place to observe birds in their natural environment and discover coastal Patagonia, not a zoo offering guaranteed encounters.

Among [Argentina](/argentina/) journeys, El Pedral stands out for combining marine wildlife with life on an old Patagonian estate. Unlike a trip devoted only to viewpoints, it is worth allowing time to walk, learn about the estancia's history and enjoy lunch when those services are included in the chosen excursion.

## Where El Pedral is and how to get there

The estancia stands near Punta Ninfas, on the approaches to Golfo Nuevo. According to El Pedral itself, it is approximately 73 km from Puerto Madryn and 100 km from Trelew Airport. Much of the approach is along a gravel road. Road conditions, wind and access arrangements need to be considered in advance.

Visits are organised by prior reservation. There may be no mobile signal at the entrance gate, making an unarranged independent arrival particularly inconvenient. For a day trip, it is sensible to agree transport and visiting times ahead of time.

On [Argentina tours](/argentina/tour/), El Pedral may be part of a longer Atlantic Patagonia itinerary. Before choosing, check whether a separate day is reserved for the colony, whether transfers are included and whether there is a stop at Punta Ninfas Lighthouse.

## When Magellanic penguins can be seen

Penguins visit the coast seasonally, so the date matters more than the appeal of the excursion's name. On one of our itineraries, the trip to the El Pedral colony is scheduled **from 15 September to 15 April**. This is a condition of that particular itinerary, not a promise that the birds will be equally active on every date within that period.

Observations differ at the start of the season, during breeding and before the birds depart. How many penguins are visible, how close visitors can get and which walking areas are accessible depend on conservation rules. You must not pick up or feed the penguins, or leave the permitted trail. Visits are designed around the colony's natural behaviour.

If wildlife is the main purpose of your trip, compare [Argentina wildlife and nature tours](/interests/wildlife/tours/argentina/). The nearby Valdés Peninsula offers other opportunities to observe marine mammals. Whale and penguin seasons overlap only in part, so dates should be chosen for your priority species.

## El Pedral or Valdés Peninsula: what is different?

| El Pedral | Valdés Peninsula |
|---|---|
| Penguin colony and estancia | Several marine wildlife observation sites |
| Punta Ninfas area | Protected area north of Puerto Madryn |
| Visit according to an agreed itinerary | Route with multiple stops |

These trips can complement each other. A visit to Valdés generally involves travel between natural sites and, in suitable conditions, whale watching. El Pedral allows you to spend much of the day in one coastal area and at the historic estancia. Combining both into one short outing without accounting for travel and visit times is not advisable.

On our 16-day "Highlights of Argentina" journey, Valdés Peninsula and El Pedral are visited on different days. The penguin excursion also takes in the Punta Ninfas area and offers an opportunity to try local food. It illustrates how to explore the Atlantic coast without rushing.

## What to bring and how to behave at the colony

Strong winds are possible along the exposed coast even in the warmer season. Closed shoes with sturdy soles, a windproof jacket, sun protection and water are useful. Layered clothing is best: coastal temperatures can feel quite different from those in town.

Keep your distance from birds, follow your guides' instructions and do not obstruct animals travelling between the land and sea. A telephoto lens is useful for photographs. Do not expect penguins to approach you at close range.

## Frequently asked questions about El Pedral

### Can El Pedral be visited in one day?

Yes. Day trips are available from the Puerto Madryn area. Departure time, transport, meals and access to the colony depend on the specific product and must be agreed before travelling.

### Will we see whales here?

Southern right whales visit Golfo Nuevo seasonally, but whale sightings are not a guaranteed outcome of a penguin excursion. If whales are your main interest, choose the appropriate season and a dedicated marine tour.

### Is El Pedral suitable for families with children?

A nature walk may suit a family if the children can follow the rules about keeping their distance from animals and manage the journey over gravel roads. Age conditions, duration and trail accessibility should be confirmed for the particular visit.

## Tours through El Pedral: Patagonian penguins on a grand journey across Argentina

[El Pedral](/argentina/place/el-pedral/) is an estancia and natural area near Punta Ninfas, south of [Puerto Madryn](/argentina/place/puerto-madryn/). Magellanic penguins nest along the rocky Atlantic coast amid the Patagonian steppe. Travellers have the opportunity to observe the birds on land in their familiar surroundings as they emerge from the sea, move about the colony and tend their nests.

Our catalogue includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} passing through El Pedral. The main option is the [16-day Highlights of Argentina tour](/argentina/tour/explore-argentina-16-days/). A separate day is devoted to the penguin colony after a visit to the marine wildlife of [Valdés Peninsula](/argentina/place/valdes-peninsula/). The journey then continues to Ushuaia, the glaciers around El Calafate and Iguazú.

## How the day at El Pedral unfolds

On the 16-day tour, the excursion is scheduled for **day 5**, while the group is based in Puerto Madryn. It is a full-day outing, not a brief stop on the way to another town. The route includes the Magellanic penguin colony, the coastal scenery and Punta Ninfas Lighthouse.

Patagonian food is also described in the itinerary: traditional roast lamb may be sampled during the excursion. Check the precise meal inclusions in the chosen tour's "Included" section. The coast is often windy and the ground beyond prepared paths can be uneven, so bring closed shoes and a wind-resistant outer layer.

El Pedral's particular appeal is its combination of wildlife and open landscapes. You see not only the birds but also their coastal habitat, where dry steppe meets the ocean and the colony follows its own seasonal cycle. Visitors observe from a distance; contact with the animals is not part of the excursion.

## How El Pedral differs from other nature stops

The preceding day of the 16-day tour takes travellers to [Valdés Peninsula](/argentina/place/valdes-peninsula/). Near [Puerto Pirámides](/argentina/place/puerto-piramides/), the itinerary includes a boat excursion to observe southern right whales; it then continues around the peninsula, passing shores frequented by elephant seals. El Pedral offers a different experience: **observing Magellanic penguins on land** is the main purpose.

| Place | Main experience |
|---|---|
| [El Pedral](/argentina/place/el-pedral/) | Penguin colony and Punta Ninfas |
| [Valdés](/argentina/place/valdes-peninsula/) | Wildlife of the peninsula |
| [Puerto Pirámides](/argentina/place/puerto-piramides/) | Seasonal whale-watching boat trip |
| [Puerto Madryn](/argentina/place/puerto-madryn/) | Base for coastal excursions |

The stops complement each other. The whale day is largely spent around the peninsula and at sea, while the penguin day centres on the colony. If wildlife observation is the main reason for choosing the tour, pay attention to **both separate dates in the itinerary**, not just photographs of whales and penguins in a general description of Patagonia.

## When to plan a penguin trip

On our itinerary, the excursion to El Pedral operates **from 15 September to 15 April**. This window matches the local operator's published day-visit season and is tied to the presence of Magellanic penguins in the colony. The same wildlife encounters cannot be promised outside this season.

Whale season around Valdés Peninsula usually runs from June to December, while boat departures depend on weather and sea conditions. To combine **El Pedral's penguins with Valdés whales**, the months when these seasonal windows overlap are particularly suitable. Even then, animals behave freely, and wind may alter boat excursions.

Take Southern Hemisphere seasons into account when choosing dates. September and October are spring; December marks the start of summer. The coast is exposed to ocean winds, so clothing suitable for a warm day in town may not be enough by the sea.

## How El Pedral fits into the 16-day itinerary

The [16-day Argentina journey](/argentina/tour/explore-argentina-16-days/) begins in [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/). Next comes the Atlantic coast: [Puerto Madryn](/argentina/place/puerto-madryn/), a day on Valdés and another at El Pedral.

After the coast, the route heads south. In [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/), travellers explore the nature of Tierra del Fuego; in [El Calafate](/argentina/place/el-calafate/), they visit Perito Moreno Glacier. The final major nature segment is devoted to Iguazú Falls. This is an option for those who want to combine penguin watching with several natural regions of Argentina, rather than making a short trip solely to the colony.

**Current tour through El Pedral:**

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_issledovanie_argentiny}}

For different combinations of regions, explore [all Argentina tours](/argentina/tour/) and [wildlife journeys](/interests/wildlife/tours/). A reference to Patagonia in another tour's name does not guarantee a visit to El Pedral; check the specific days.

## What to check before choosing an itinerary

For a penguin-focused journey, the main constraint is seasonality. The 16-day tour includes the day at El Pedral in its main itinerary, but the exact excursion, meals and transfers must be checked in that tour's listing. The conditions of standalone excursions run by other operators should not automatically be applied to Ada Tours.

Consider the pace of the journey as well. After several days in Buenos Aires and on the coast, the trip continues with flights and transfers to other parts of Argentina. Travellers who want to spend the maximum possible time with marine animals may want to compare the [9-day wildlife tour through Patagonia and Iberá](/argentina/tour/argentina-wildlife-buenos-aires/). The latter includes whales and Valdés, but **does not list El Pedral in its published itinerary**.

## Frequently asked questions

### Can penguins be seen at El Pedral year-round?

No. The selected tour specifies a visit to the colony between 15 September and 15 April. At other times, birdwatching must be planned differently.

### How long does a visit to El Pedral take?

The [16-day itinerary](/argentina/tour/explore-argentina-16-days/) allows a full excursion day for the site, departing from Puerto Madryn. Exact return hours are not fixed in the published description.

### Is whale watching scheduled for the same day?

No. The published itinerary places the Valdés visit and boat trip from Puerto Pirámides on the previous day. The penguin colony has its own excursion day.

### Can visitors approach penguins closely?

Birds may be observed from a relatively short distance, but they must not be touched or chased. Visitors follow the site's rules and designated route.

### Is there a tour visiting only El Pedral rather than all of Argentina?

This catalogue shows published **tours that pass through the destination**. A standalone one-day trip cannot be assumed to be part of Ada Tours' range without a separately confirmed product. Use the table above to choose an existing itinerary.

## Ensenada Zaratiegui: seashore views and the Costera coastal trail

Ensenada Zaratiegui is a bay on the Beagle Channel in [Tierra del Fuego National Park](/argentina/place/tierra-del-fuego-national-park/), near [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/). Its pebbled shore, dark water and forested hillsides reveal the maritime side of Tierra del Fuego. Redonda Island lies opposite.

It is a destination in its own right on a short sightseeing drive. For hikers, Ensenada is the starting point of the Costera trail. There is a major difference between a brief walk by the water and a multi-hour trek, so decide on the format in advance.

## A short stroll or 8 kilometres along the coast

The **Costera** trail starts from the Ensenada Zaratiegui parking area and follows the shore to the junction of National Route 3 with the road to [Lake Roca (Acigami)](/argentina/place/lago-roca/). The park administration gives a distance of **8 km**, an estimated time of **4 hours** and a moderate difficulty rating. Its usual opening season is **November to April**, although access may vary.

There is also a shorter woodland route, **Cruce Ruta 3 — Ensenada**, approximately **1.3 km** long. It takes around 40 minutes and runs between trees parallel to the road. This is a separate walk, not a replacement for Costera.

| Option | What to allow for |
|---|---|
| Bay shoreline | A short sightseeing stop |
| Forest trail | 1.3 km and about 40 minutes |
| Costera | 8 km and about 4 hours |

If you choose Costera, arrange your return transport in advance, as the trail ends at a different location. Carry water, food, shoes with dependable grip and windproof clothing. Even without major elevation changes, a long coastal walk requires stamina.

## What to visit alongside Ensenada

[Lapataia Bay](/argentina/place/lapataia-bay/) is known for the end of National Route 3 and short boardwalks by the water. At the [Pipo River](/argentina/place/pipo-river/), you can see the rocky riverbed and, when trails are open, walk to a waterfall. Ensenada stands out for its sea views and the opportunity to spend much of the day on a coastal hike.

On our [14-day Ada Tours itinerary](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-14-days/), the bay is part of a national park sightseeing day together with Lapataia, the Pipo River and Lake Roca. **This does not mean that the four-hour Costera hike is included in the tour:** the full trail must be arranged separately if it fits the programme.

## Weather and seasonality

Wind and cool conditions are common on the exposed shore of the Beagle Channel. Rain protection and closed shoes are useful even for a short stop; for trekking, allow extra time for the return. Avoid venturing onto wet rocks close to the waves just to take a photograph.

The officially stated Costera season is November to April. Before setting out, check the trail's status with the park and review the weather forecast. If the trail is closed, choose permitted viewpoints or another walk.

## Frequently asked questions about Ensenada Zaratiegui

### Where is Ensenada Zaratiegui?

On the Beagle Channel coast within [Tierra del Fuego National Park](/argentina/place/tierra-del-fuego-national-park/).

### Do I need to complete Costera to see the bay?

No. The bay can be enjoyed as a short stop without a multi-hour hike.

### When is Costera open?

The official description gives November to April. Check for any specific restrictions before hiking.

### Can Ensenada be combined with Lapataia?

Yes, on a sightseeing visit to the park. If taking the full Costera hike, it is better to reduce the number of other stops.

## Tours through Ensenada Zaratiegui: choosing an itinerary

**If you want to see Ensenada Zaratiegui, start by looking at the Tierra del Fuego National Park programme.** The bay lies on the Beagle Channel amid the forests and mountains of Tierra del Fuego. Travellers usually come from [Ushuaia](/argentina/place/ushuaia/) on an excursion to [Tierra del Fuego National Park](/argentina/place/tierra-del-fuego-national-park/).

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}}. The bay is included in the structured geography of these itineraries, but **the descriptions of the actual stop differ**. On one tour Ensenada is expressly listed among the places visited on the excursion day. On the other, only the national park excursion as a whole is mentioned. This distinction matters if you particularly want to walk along the shore.

For more about the bay's nature and location, see the [Ensenada Zaratiegui page](/argentina/place/ensenada-zaratiegui/). Below, we compare the practical elements of each journey: the park day, nights in Ushuaia, neighbouring regions and excursion format.

## Two itineraries featuring Tierra del Fuego

| Tour | Main difference |
|---|---|
| [Ice, Sun and the End of the World, 12 days](/multi-country/tour/argentina-brazil-private-tour-12-days/) | Iguazú and Rio |
| [Best of Argentina, 14 days](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-14-days/) | Bariloche and Iguazú |

### Ice, Sun and the End of the World: from glaciers to Rio

The [12-day Argentina and Brazil tour](/multi-country/tour/argentina-brazil-private-tour-12-days/) has scheduled dates of **28 February to 11 March 2027**. The journey starts in [Buenos Aires](/argentina/place/buenos-aires/), then continues to [Perito Moreno Glacier](/argentina/place/perito-moreno-glacier/) and Tierra del Fuego. **2 nights** are planned in Ushuaia.

On day six there is a group excursion through the national park with an English-speaking guide. Ensenada Zaratiegui is included among the main destinations of the route, but **the description of this particular excursion day does not explicitly list a stop at the bay**. Travellers wishing to step ashore at Ensenada should confirm the precise order of stops before choosing this tour.

After Ushuaia, the itinerary continues to Iguazú Falls on both sides of the border and finishes in Rio de Janeiro. The route connects glacial Patagonia, the Beagle Channel coast, subtropical forests and the ocean. Domestic flights and certain optional activities have their own payment terms, listed on the tour page.

### Best of Argentina: the bay is explicitly on the itinerary

On the [14-day tour featuring Bariloche and Iguazú](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-14-days/), the national park is visited on **day seven**. The programme lists the stops in detail: the Pipo River, Mount Susana, Ensenada Bay with views of Redonda Island, [Lake Roca (Acigami)](/argentina/place/lago-roca/) and [Lapataia Bay](/argentina/place/lapataia-bay/). This is a group excursion with an English-speaking guide. The trip also includes **2 nights** in Ushuaia.

After Tierra del Fuego, the journey continues to [Bariloche](/argentina/place/bariloche/) among the lakes and mountains of northern Patagonia, then heads to Iguazú. **If an explicitly scheduled stop at Ensenada matters to you, the second tour gives a more definite description.** The first will appeal more to those interested in Rio, confirmed 2027 dates and the transition from glaciers to the tropics.

## How a bay visit differs from exploring the whole park

Tierra del Fuego National Park encompasses seacoast, forests, lakes and river valleys. Sightseeing drives generally include several stops at natural sites. A short photo stop at the bay and an independent walk along the coastal trail, however, require very different amounts of time.

Argentina's government tourism information mentions about 40 km of marked trails in the park. During one excursion day, travellers can see several contrasting areas, but the entire trail network is **not automatically included** in every tour itinerary.

For a first visit, a good combination is Ensenada Bay, [Lake Roca](/argentina/place/lago-roca/) and [Lapataia](/argentina/place/lapataia-bay/), as on the 14-day itinerary. Ensenada offers views of the Beagle Channel, Lake Roca offers freshwater and wooded slopes, and Lapataia offers a bay and mountain valleys. If a long walk is your priority, discuss the duration of the stop and access to the chosen section in advance.

## When to plan a tour through Ensenada

Tierra del Fuego is known for cool, windy and changeable weather. A windproof jacket, sturdy shoes and a warm layer are advisable for visiting the bay even during the Southern Hemisphere summer. Winds on the Beagle Channel coast feel stronger than among the buildings of Ushuaia.

There is also a seasonal restriction: Argentina's government tourism website states that **access to Ensenada closes from May to September**. This does not mean the entire national park closes; other routes remain available depending on conditions. For a particular departure, check access to the bay and the chosen trail.

The [Ice, Sun and the End of the World tour](/multi-country/tour/argentina-brazil-private-tour-12-days/) takes place in late February and early March 2027. The other itinerary's visiting opportunities depend on the dates selected. Check the combination of seasonality, excursion availability and connections between regions.

## Comparing inclusions and itinerary intensity

Both tours include a group excursion to the national park with an English-speaking guide, but their wider routes and packages differ. Compare the sequence of days rather than just one stop: time in Ushuaia, arrival and departure dates, optional activities and which flights are included in the price.

**The 12-day tour** goes from Tierra del Fuego to Iguazú and Rio. **The 14-day tour** includes a separate stage in Bariloche, followed by both sides of Iguazú. For travellers interested in lake landscapes and excursions in the southern Andes, the second offers more variety within Argentina. The first is better suited to combining Patagonia with famous sights in Brazil.

To spend more time in Tierra del Fuego itself, compare published options in the [Argentina tour catalogue](/argentina/tour/) and [Argentina nature tours](/interests/wildlife/tours/argentina/). The [Ushuaia page](/argentina/place/ushuaia/) can also help with choosing other regional trips. Remember that inclusion of another natural attraction does not confirm a visit to Ensenada Bay.

## Frequently asked questions

### Do all tours in the catalogue explicitly promise a stop at the bay?

No. On the [14-day itinerary](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-14-days/), Ensenada is expressly named in the national park day. On the [12-day programme](/multi-country/tour/argentina-brazil-private-tour-12-days/), the bay is associated with the route, but the day description refers to a national park excursion without naming the bay separately.

### Can Ensenada, Lapataia and Lake Roca be combined?

Yes. This combination is included in the [14-day trip](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-14-days/). Several natural areas are visited in sequence during one excursion day. Time at each stop depends on the group's schedule.

### How many nights are planned in Ushuaia?

Both of the compared tours specify **2 nights in Ushuaia**. This makes it possible to dedicate a day to the national park. Adding another excursion depends on available free time and the programme terms.

### Which route should I choose for Rio de Janeiro?

[Ice, Sun and the End of the World](/multi-country/tour/argentina-brazil-private-tour-12-days/) finishes in Rio after Patagonia, Ushuaia and Iguazú. [Best of Argentina](/multi-country/tour/best-of-argentina-14-days/) includes Bariloche and its lake scenery instead of Rio.

### Is Ensenada accessible in the winter months?

According to the official tourism information, access to the bay is closed between May and September. Check the specific stop's status before travelling: the national park may be operating while access to Ensenada is restricted.
